ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all general partners, officials, authorized agents, and UBOs holding ≥25% interests against: (a) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act (S.C. 1992, c. 17) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (S.C. 2001, c. 33); (b) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (c) US OFAC/SDN List (as policy overlay for USD transactions); and (d) automated PEP database plus adverse-media hits. Enhanced due diligence required for any partner connected to high-risk jurisdictions (FATF grey/black list) or involving DNFBPs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online Portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The partnership name must be in French; a non-French name is permitted only if a recognized French version or if it consists of a trademark and is registered accordingly; the name must be drafted in Latin/Roman characters and any foreign script must be transliterated into French phonetics. The Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business (CQLR c. C-11, r. 9) require French descriptions on public documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Canada' or any name suggesting a relationship with the Government of Canada (requires prior federal authorization)
'Québec' or any name suggesting provincial affiliation (requires government approval)
'Bank', 'Banque', 'Trust', 'Trust Company', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Reinsurance' (regulatory license from the Autorité des marchés financiers required)
'University', 'College', 'Institute of Technology' (prior consent of the Ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur)
'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.' (not appropriate for a limited partnership unless such words form part of an approved corporate name previously owned and capable of transfer)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name rejection appeal: (1) Applicant receives a 'Refusal Notice' from REQ stating the statutory ground for refusal. (2) Within 30 days, applicant may file a written request for review with the Inspecteur général des institutions financières (IGIF) (or directly with REQ's internal review service) accompanied by a detailed name-analysis brief and any consent letters from regulators. (3) The reviewing officer may render a decision within 20 business days. (4) If the refusal is maintained, applicant may apply to the Court of Québec for limited judicial review (Art. 529 C.p.c.) or file a new name request with a revised name. Name reservations are not extendable but can be renewed by filing a fresh reservation request before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not independently sufficient for a Quebec limited partnership; a physical and registered office in Quebec is required, and the registered office may be a commercial address maintained by a licensed corporate agent provided that it is not merely a mail-drop. For a SaaS analytics business with no physical premises, the use of a 'bureau virtuel' plus a contractual agreement with a local trust/agent for record location and service of process is generally accepted by REQ.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk (estimated <5% per year): Revenu Québec and the Registraire des entreprises do not routinely conduct unannounced on-site inspections of registered LPs in the MarTech sector; physical audits are more likely in respect of payroll or sales tax presence, but a pure SaaS/analytics entity with remote operations will face negligible inspection frequency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Book IV, Title III, Limited Partnerships (arts. 2236–2272 C.c.Q.); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), arts. 2, 21, 54–57; Regulation respecting the fees of the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), 2050 rue de Bleury, Montréal, Québec, acting under the supervision of the Inspecteur général des institutions financières (IGIF).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in accordance with art. 21 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership. Contributions are freely fixed by the partnership agreement and may consist of money, property, or services for the general partner; a limited partner must contribute money or property only (art. 2259 C.c.Q.). No escrow account or capital deposit is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — GENERAL PARTNER OF [●] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (LP): RESOLVED, that the General Partner adopts the Partnership Agreement of [●] Limited Partnership, effective [●], and approves the subscription of partnership units by the initial Limited Partners, with contributions set out in Schedule A. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the principal establishment and registered office shall be located at [●], [city], Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec shall record such address. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed Authorized Representative and Operations Manager, empowered to effect statutory filings, open banking accounts, engage employees, and execute client agreements. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the signing officers are authorized to do all things incidental to the foregoing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation with the Quebec Enterprise Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online reservation module (Registraire en ligne)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary distinctiveness search in the enterprise register for the proposed LP name (French version recommended, e.g., '[●] S.E.C.'). File a Déclaration de réservation de nom (Name Reservation Declaration) electronically through Registraire en ligne, paying the reservation fee ($36 CAD for a 90-day hold). The name must contain a legal element indicating limited partnership status (e.g., 'Limited Partnership' or 'S.E.C.') and must not create confusion with existing registered names.
required_dossiers: Proposed name (French/English)
Name search report or database screenshot
Applicant identification (general partner)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new reservation with a revised distinctive component or seek a review by the Inspecteur général des institutions financières (IGIF) within 30 days of the refusal notice; the IGIF may waive the confusion ground in limited cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Constitutional Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary (notaire) or in-house legal counsel; no governmental filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the contrat de société (limited partnership agreement) under arts. 2236–2272 C.c.Q. The deed must name the general partner (with unlimited liability) and limited partners, define capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management and agency powers, withdrawal and admission mechanisms, and the non-management restriction for limited partners. Execute in private writing; notarization is optional but advisable for third-party bank and registry purposes. If the general partner is a corporation, hold its shareholder/board meeting and produce a signed resolution.
required_dossiers: Signed Limited Partnership Agreement
Schedule of contributions (capital, property, money)
Corporate resolution of general partner (if corporate)
Copies of identification documents of partners
Domicile/addresses of all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify omissions or ambiguities by executing an amending agreement (avenant) at any time; if a third party contests the partnership's existence, a declaratory judgement of the Superior Court of Québec may be sought, and the partnership remains valid for acts performed before cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration — Filing of the Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Registraire en ligne (https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the electronic filing portal, select 'Déclaration d'immatriculation — société en commandite', and complete the form: legal name, NEQ (Quebec enterprise number, auto-assigned or from reservation), principal establishment address in Quebec, nature of activities (NAICS 541511 — Custom Computer Programming / SEO analytics), identity and domicile of the general partner and limited partners, capital contributions, date of constitution, period of existence, and the LP's representative. Attach the executed partnership agreement and pay the CAD $36 online filing fee (equivalent of approx. USD $26). Upon approval the Registraire issues a Certificate of Registration and the authoritative NEQ.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic registration declaration
Name reservation certificate (if applicable)
Scanned partnership agreement
Proof of principal establishment address (lease or utility bill)
NAICS/ISIC activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or returned, file an amending declaration (déclaration modificative) correcting the defects within the registry's stated timeline; refusal decisions may be appealed to the Superior Court of Québec or to the IGIF under art. 105.1 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Tax Accounts with Revenu Québec and CRA (QST, GST/HST, Payroll)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — Mon dossier d'entreprise online portal; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ obtained at registration, open a Revenu Québec file and register for Québec Sales Tax (QST), the harmonized GST/QST if applicable, employer source deductions (income tax, QPIP, CNESST assessment) and QPIP retirement accounts if employees will be hired. Simultaneously, register the LP for GST/HST with the CRA under its business number (BN) if taxable SaaS revenue is expected to exceed the $30,000 CAD threshold. Designate an authorized representative (mandant/mandataire) for filing compliance in both portals. Confirm the effective start-of-supply date of the SEO content analytics service to align the first return period.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate
Certificate of Registration of the LP
List of partners (name, address, SIN/BN where needed)
Mandate forms (RM-10 for Revenu Québec; RC59 for CRA)
Bank account confirmation (to be provided after bank opening)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is not processed within the SLA, escalate through the business portal help desk with the NEQ's transaction number; Revenu Québec and the CRA may backdate the effective registration to the date the partnership first made taxable supplies, provided the LP submits a written explanation and supporting contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Establishment Permit and CNESST Occupational Health & Safety Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permitting office (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Permis en ligne service) and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business permit (permis de commerce / permis d'établissement) for the registered office if the municipal zoning or vigilance by-law requires a permit for technology/office activities; pay the municipal tariff. Register the establishment with the CNESST within 60 days of hiring the first employee; provide the payroll estimate for industry classification (information and cultural industries rate). If more than 20 workers, adopt a prevention program (programme de prévention) and health and safety committee structure. For the SaaS analytics tool, no specific industrial clearance is required, but a desk/IT load electrical certificate may be requested by the landlord.
required_dossiers: Municipal business permit application
Proof of NEQ / registration certificate
Lease agreement or proof of ownership
CNESST employer registration form (incl. payroll projection)
Attestation of workplace first aid and fire safety compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit is denied, file an appeal with the municipal council's permit review committee or the zoning interpretation officer within 15 days; for CNESST classification disputes, submit a review application to the CNESST provincial board within 30 days and continue operations under the provisional rate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) — no industrial-sector approval applies to ISIC 6201 software/analytics enterprises; no manufacturing license is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no provincial 'autorisation ministérielle' is required for a search engine optimization (SEO) data crawler and keyword analytics SaaS provider under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises or the Loi sur la qualité de l'environnement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — CATEGORY 'REGISTRATION-NOT-REQUIRED'. The dry-office MarTech SaaS activity does not fall under the mandatory environmental impact assessment (EIA) regime of Schedule I of the Règlement relatif à l'évaluation et l'examen des impacts sur l'environnement (REIE), nor the Registre des activités de redevances; no 'Avis de conformité' declaration is required for software-only operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge: no wastewater, VOCs, or atmospheric contaminants generated by code development and data analytics. If voluntary IT equipment/co-location exists, comply with municipal e-waste (RECYC-QUÉBEC) directives and the Règlement sur la récupération et la valorisation de produits; server rooms must respect electrical safety standards (CSA C22.1) and thermal-load ventilation requirements of the Quebec Construction Code. Greenhouse gas reporting thresholds (Déclaration annuelle des émissions de GES — MELCCFP) do not apply below 10,000 tCO2e/year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire safety certificate or attestation of conformity per the Règlement sur la sécurité incendie (Quebec Fire Safety Regulation) for the registered office fit-out; structural load inspection if server racks/load-bearing installations exceed office floor capacity; occupational clearance: register with the CNESST and carry out a hazard identification; maintain first-aid boxes, safety signage and an emergency evacuation plan; for premises with 20+ employees, adopt a workplace health and safety program under the LSST (Loi sur la santé et la sécurité du travail) and establish a joint committee.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), GST/HST program and International Tax Services Office, portal: CRA 'My Business Account' and Business Registration Online (BRO); and Revenu Québec, portal: 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'. For a business with a permanent establishment in Quebec, the federal GST/HST is administered and collected by Revenu Québec under the Canada-Quebec Tax Collection Agreement, while the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) is a separate provincial VAT administered solely by Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Register the Limited Partnership in the Quebec enterprise register (Registraire d'entreprises) to obtain the provincial 'Numéro d'entreprise du Québec' (NEQ), filing the declaration of a limited partnership or amendment identifying the general partner. STEP 2: Apply to the CRA for the federal Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST account via Form RC1 or Business Registration Online, indicating a Quebec permanent establishment and attaching the partnership agreement extracts that designate the representative partner. STEP 3: Register separately with Revenu Québec for the QST account (account type 'RM') after confirming that the LP has ceased to qualify as a small supplier or expects to exceed the threshold; Revenu Québec requires the NEQ, the BN, the RC1 reference number, and particulars of non-resident partners for the TIN/QST cross-reference. STEP 4: Execute the statutory election under ETA s. 273(1) appointing the general partner as representative for GST/HST and QST administration, and file the applicable Revenu Québec e-registration declaration. STEP 5: Obtain the CRA confirmation letter and the Revenu Québec registration certificate, then begin issuing invoices carrying the BN, GST/HST registration number, and QST registration number; total processing time is typically 2 to 10 business days. Non-resident registrants without a Canadian residence may use the CRA International Tax Services Office and Revenu Québec's non-resident unit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a domestic check-the-box classification regime for limited partnerships. The relevant statutory elections available to this LP are: (i) ETA s. 273(1) election designating a partner as the representative for the partnership's GST/HST and QST registration, filing, and payment obligations; (ii) ITA s. 96(1.1) and (1.2) elections fixing the allocation of partnership income and losses among partners independent of the distribution year; (iii) ITA s. 216 election by a non-resident partner to file a Part I Canadian income tax return with respect to taxable Canadian income from the LP rather than being subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding; (iv) corresponding QST Act elections made to Revenu Québec aligning the GST/HST and QST registration and filing framework; and (v) for US federal tax purposes only, an IRC s. 7701 check-the-box election permitting the Canadian LP to be disregarded or treated as an association taxable as a corporation, which has no effect on the Canadian or Quebec tax classification of the entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) combined with the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) - a dual VAT system applicable to taxable supplies of SEO-content analytics SaaS services made in or consumed in Quebec, administered jointly by Revenu Québec under the tax collection agreement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in a calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters triggers mandatory registration for both GST/HST (ETA small supplier rule, s. 148(4)) and QST (parallel rule under the QST Act). For a non-resident LP not carrying on business in Canada, the same CAD 30,000 threshold is measured on worldwide taxable supplies; once the LP's taxable supplies made through a Quebec establishment or deemed made in Quebec under the place-of-supply rules for digital services exceed CAD 30,000, registration with Revenu Québec for QST and the GST/HST becomes compulsory. An LP whose only Canadian supplies are zero-rated exports may elect to register even below the threshold to claim input tax refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada or Quebec for SaaS analytics services. Electronic filing is mandatory for registered persons: GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE XML/API (Biz2File) and QST returns through Revenu Québec's electronic services. Invoicing must comply with the ETA and QST record-keeping rules (seller and recipient identification, registration numbers, date, description, tax consideration, rate applied, or zero-rating indication), and all records must be retained for six years. Revenu Québec has announced under its enterprise tax modernization project (Quebec Budget 2025-2026) a phased mandatory business-to-business e-invoicing regime intended to apply to large businesses (annual turnover above CAD 10 million) in the late 2020s; no such obligation is currently in force for this LP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electrononic_invoicing_and_clearance_man: This field name is internally corrected to 'electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_mandate' as per the governing schema; content is stated above.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under the ETA Schedule VI, Part V, ss. 1 to 3 where tangible personal property is exported from Canada in accordance with the statutory export evidence rules. Services and digital products (the LP's SEO analytics SaaS): zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 where the recipient is a non-resident of Canada, is not registered under the ETA at the time the supply is made, and the service is not rendered in respect of real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or a service enjoyed or performed in Canada; the place-of-supply rules in ETA s. 144.1 and the corresponding QST place-of-supply rules determine whether the supply is made in Canada. For QST, supplies that are zero-rated under the ETA are correspondingly zero-rated under the QST Act unless specifically recharacterized by Quebec. The vendor must evidence non-residence through the subscription contract, billing address, IP/geolocation logs, and payment-rail records (Stripe/Paddle) demonstrating that the customer's use and enjoyment occurred outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For goods: Canadian Export Declaration filed electronically with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian export reporting system, including Form B13A for controlled goods; the Customs Act and Export Control List commodity classifications must be reflected

For goods: original transport document proving exportation - ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or road manifest (CMR) - naming the Canadian vendor as exporter; for pure digital/SaaS supplies this is substituted by server access and session logs evidencing offshore geolocation and foreign use of the platform

Commercial invoice, executed SaaS subscription agreement, and customer non-residence declaration showing the application of the 0% rate, the foreign billing address, the customer's status as a non-registered non-resident, and the LP's GST/HST and QST registration numbers

Inward remittance evidence: Canada does not issue a formal 'Inward Remittance Certificate'; the accepted substitute is the bank statement, SWIFT transfer advice, or payment-rail settlement report (Stripe/Paddle) evidencing receipt of funds from abroad within the documented period
Internal zero-rating substantiation worksheet cross-referencing the statutory provision relied upon and the six-year retention file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess beyond the normal three-year period (four years for QST) where zero-rating is claimed on the basis of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud; fraudulent export zero-rating attracts penalties of 25% for gross negligence and up to 200% of the tax evaded for wilful evasion, under ETA ss. 280 and 285, with compounded daily interest; criminal prosecution under ETA ss. 327 and 328 and ITA s. 239 may result in fines up to CAD 200,000 or between 100% and 200% of the tax sought, plus imprisonment up to five years. Revenu Québec applies parallel penalty and interest provisions under the QST Act and the Taxation Act and may jointly void registrations, demand immediate payment of reassessed net tax, and pursue the general partner personally where the LP is used as a facade. Although no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline exists in Canada, the 180-day benchmark is maintained as a prudent compliance standard; remittance evidence gathered after that date may be treated as weakening the documentation chain and can justify denial of the zero-rating, reopening of the limitation period, and clawback of input tax credits previously refunded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada maintains an open capital account and does not operate a dedicated foreign exchange administration body. Prudential supervision of federally incorporated banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/ATF regulation in FINTRAC, and payment-system oversight in Payments Canada. Commercial bank onboarding and foreign-currency operations are governed by the Bank Act, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and applicable provincial consumer-protection statutes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full, unrestricted convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. No exchange-control approvals, registration, or prior authorizations apply to inbound capital injections, foreign-currency financing, or repatriation of profits through distributions from a Quebec limited partnership. The sole material impediment to profit remittance is tax-driven: under section 194 of the Income Tax Act (Canada), a partnership that credits or pays income to a non-resident partner must withhold Part XIII tax of 25%, subject to treaty reduction (e.g., 15% under the Canada-US Convention for the portion treated as a distribution to a US resident beneficial owner) or a section 115 net-basis election arrangement. Subsections 216 and 217 elections are available for specific income classes but would typically not be the operative route for SaaS business income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds, including software subscriptions, SEO data-crawler licensing, or analytics-as-a-service revenue. The partnership may retain USD and other foreign-currency balances in Canadian or offshore accounts without Bank of Canada or OSFI authorization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD) plus a segregated Capital Escrow Account for partner contributions
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with BMO EBiz transaction settlement and cross-border treasury desk
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with RBC Express for SWIFT origination and USD correspondent clearing
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with mirroring capability to TD Bank N.A. for US-side receivables concentration
Operational Account (CAD/USD) via CIBC US dollar clearing network

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Group (Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec) — regulated credit-union cooperative
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Operating Account (CAD) plus US Currency Business Account with treasury FX desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — permissible only as a complementary collection and FX-conversion rail, never as the primary treasury account provider. The European-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licence is not recognized in Canada; global fintech firms (Wise Platform, Airwallex, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury) must operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under PCMLTFA and are not authorized to accept demand deposits like Schedule I banks. A Quebec LP may lawfully use such platforms to receive USD payouts from Paddle or Stripe and to convert currency at commercial rates, but the capital escrow account, statutory distribution clearing, and operating liquidity must ultimately reside with a Canadian regulated bank to preserve LVTS/Real-Time Rail access and to avoid isolated PCMLTFA facilitation risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under PCMLTFA client-identification rules for low-risk non-privileged corporate clients, and neither the Bank of Canada nor OSFI mandates an in-person general-partner interview. In practice, Quebec Schedule I banks require remote video identification of every signing officer, certified true copies of partnership formation documents, and notarized corporate resolutions; an in-person appearance in Quebec may be required only where the bank demands a signature guarantee or security acknowledgment before a notary. Non-resident directors can ordinarily open the account without coming to Canada, subject to enhanced due diligence when the ultimate beneficial owner is not a resident of a recognized FATF jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident multi-tier beneficial ownership (foreign PE fund, US LLC feeder, or offshore holding layer) without a transparent ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership-structure chart; Certificate of Limited Partnership and Declaration of Registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ); certified partnership agreement; KYC forms identifying each individual with 10% or greater ownership; passport and 90-day proof of address for each such individual; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements; registrar extract from the ultimate-parent jurisdiction; audited or reviewed financial statements of the general partner; and applicable trust- or fund-governance documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High recurring volumes of small-ticket US SaaS subscription receipts flowing through Stripe/Paddle without matching operational expenditures, creating an unanchored receivable pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard-form SaaS subscription agreement; monthly recurring revenue (MRR) ledger; sample invoices; billing and pricing page documentation; payment-processor payout statements for the prior 3-6 months; subscriber-count and traffic-analytics dashboard reports; narrative diagram of the SEO crawler and keyword-analytics engine architecture proving bona fide commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax registration mismatch — absence of GST/HST (CRA) and QST (Revenu Québec) accounts for a revenue-generating analytics business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA GST/HST account registration confirmation and Revenu Québec QST registration certificate; account-status letters; and, where zero-rating for exports is claimed, supporting customer-country documentation and the underlying export contracts proving the supply is made to non-residents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-tripping typology: capital deposit followed quickly by a distribution to a foreign partner, with no evidence of business deployment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital commitment agreement with capital-call schedule; bank funding records; GP resolutions approving the investment program; cash-flow forecast; SaaS cost build-up (hosting, data-collection infrastructure, payroll); and a Part XIII withholding compliance file including completed W-8BEN-E or NR301 forms for each non-resident partner to demonstrate that treaty-reduced withholding has been correctly calculated.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions should be remitted by the partner via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire where same-day USD settlement is required) directly to the LP's CAD or USD account at a Quebec Schedule I bank, with a payment narrative reading 'Capital Contribution - [investor name] - [LP name] - NEQ [registration number]' and an ISO 20022 purpose code of 'CAPC' (capital payment). The bank is required to report any electronic transfer of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, so the partnership must retain the capital commitment letter, the confirmation copy of the MT103, and the capital-account entry to allow seamless audit. USD-to-CAD conversion may be executed with the account bank as a deliverable spot or forward outright; no prior Bank of Canada clearance, licence, or repatriation filing is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade and operating settlements, the recommended clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border vendor and contractor payments, with ISO purpose code 'TRAD' or 'SUPP' and the corresponding invoice reference; (ii) domestic CAD clearing through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for Canadian suppliers; (iii), commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are not necessary for a recurring SaaS licensing model but remain available if the SEO-data-crawler hardware or colocation contracts require documentary settlement; (iv) distribution remittances to US partners should be executed by MT103 with purpose code 'DIVP' and accompanied by a withholding evidence package proving Part XIII treaty-reduced tax compliance; and (v) Stripe and Paddle sales receipts should be instructed to settle in USD into the LP's USD sub-account to eliminate embedded FX spreads on each payout.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (plain vanilla and average-rate forwards) for hedging USD-denominated subscription receivables from Stripe/Paddle, executed with the account bank under an ISDA 2002 or Canadian Master Agreement with typical tenors of up to 24 months
FX options (European-style calls and puts) and zero-cost collars structured on USD-to-CAD conversion of forecast revenue
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) where a partner loan or intercompany financing is extended in USD against CAD operating liquidity, executed under an ISDA 2002 Collateral Annex

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in Canada but are economically redundant for CAD/USD, and would be considered only for ancillary exposure to non-convertible emerging-market currencies that arise from the SEO analytics tool's multi-currency invoicing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Québec Enterprise Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the anniversary date of original registration (within the month immediately preceding the anniversary). A new declaration must be filed every year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing places the partnership in default; penalties apply (approximately CAD $19 to $50 per partner/director). Non-filing for two consecutive years triggers administrative cancellation of registration (strike-off) and dissolution of the limited partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Income Information Return (including financial statements and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Revenu Québec for provincial data sharing where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (generally March 31 for calendar-year partnerships; extended to August 31 for some fiscal periods)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: CAD $25 per partner per month (minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500). Subsequent failure to file may result in criminal prosecution summary conviction penalties and additional compliance orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for a Quebec limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Mandatory audit arises only if: (i) the partnership agreement expressly requires an audit; (ii) the partnership is a reporting issuer under securities legislation; or (iii) a regulated financial covenant or creditor imposes an audit requirement. Small private LPs customarily rely on reviewed/compiled financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE depending on whether the partnership is publicly accountable; ordinary private LPs generally apply ASPE under Canadian GAAP (CPA Canada Handbook).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to REQ must confirm the identity, address, and percentage share of each limited and general partner. Any transfer of partnership units or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with REQ within 15 days of the change. In addition, the partnership's internal register of partners must be updated independently for any share/unit transfer, with no statutory filing fee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners, showing capital contributions and profit share percentages)
Register of General Partner(s) (equivalent to register of directors for an LP, identifying each general partner and their registered office)
Minute Book (records of partnership resolutions and consents, if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200 – $1,200 USD per year in Quebec for registered office and statutory agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 – $12,000 USD per year for a typical early-stage SaaS limited partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%) general corporate rate; the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level corporate income tax, with income allocated to partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Canada/Quebec. Preferential regimes include: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income, combined effective ~12.2%); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs); Quebec innovation tax credits for technology SME; reduction for manufacturing and processing profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 (Partnership Information Return) – Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) electronic filing via approved EFILER software or CRA Internet File Transfer; no NETFILE option for this return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 return must be filed within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end; T5013 slips must be provided to partners by March 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I – Identification and fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, business number (BN), address, fiscal year-end, jurisdiction of formation (Quebec, Canada), and general partner identifiers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident partners and their jurisdiction of residence; attach any non-resident partner election to file under Part I on Canadian-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues from SaaS subscriptions, SEO data licensing, and analytics tool charges; deduct allowable expenses (employee salaries, cloud infrastructure, R&D, professional fees, office overhead).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Canadian-source revenue to non-resident partners; deduct only expenses connected to Canadian-source business income; maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for cross-border intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 – Allocation of income/loss to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit-sharing ratio distributed among general and limited partners, including each partner's share of taxable income/loss, capital gains/losses, and resource-related expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate each non-resident partner's allocable share of Canadian-source income; CRA may require Form NR304 (Election under Section 216) for certain income, and non-resident partners may be subject to Part I tax on a net basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 3 – Reconciliation of accounting to fiscal income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of net accounting income to taxable income, including adjustments for non-deductible expenses, tax reserves, and capital cost allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, state deemed Canadian-source amounts and any Part XIII withholding credits available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty for T5013: CAD 25/day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500. Failure to issue T5013 slips: CAD 100 per slip (minimum), up to CAD 7,500 for intentional omissions. Knowingly false statements: additional penalties up to CAD 5,000 and criminal liability under Income Tax Act s.239 (imprisonment up to 5 years).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: TP-600 (Partnership Return) – Revenu Québec (SODEC / e-CO electronic transmission; paper only if authorized).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: TP-600 must be filed within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal period end; TP-600 slips to partners are due March 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), legal name, address, fiscal period, and partnership type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate whether the partnership has an establishment outside Quebec and whether non-resident partners are deemed to be carrying on business in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenues, expenses, and net income/loss computed under Quebec Taxation Act; SaaS revenue recognized when earned; cloud hosting and bandwidth costs deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limit deduction of cross-border head-office charges to arm's length amounts; non-resident partners may claim Quebec income tax abroad as a foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partners' shares of income/loss and Quebec-source taxable income for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter each non-resident partner's share of Quebec-source business income; Quebec may require the partnership to withhold tax when income is distributed to non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late filing penalty: CAD 25/day, maximum CAD 2,500; failure to provide TP-600 slips: CAD 100 per slip (minimum), up to CAD 2,500; intentional false declaration: penalty up to CAD 5,000 plus prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder. Treaty-reduced rates: e.g., Canada-US Treaty 15% portfolio / 5% for shareholdings of at least 30% voting control; Canada-UK Treaty often 15% / 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and file CRA Form NR301 (Statement of Entitlement to Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) with the Canadian payer before payment, accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the resident country's tax authority. For income allocated through a Quebec LP, Form NR302 (Statement of Entitlement to Benefits Under a Tax Treaty for a Partnership) is used where the partnership is treated as transparent in Canada but opaque in the partner's jurisdiction. The withholding agent must retain NR301/NR302, TRC, partnership agreement, and limitation-on-benefits documentation for six years. CRA may grant an advance waiver for interest/royalty payments where treaty relief is not straightforward.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents: statutory 25% Part XIII, with typical treaty rate 10% for industrial royalties and 0% for certain copyright/brand royalties. Interest: statutory 25% for non-arm's-length or participating debt; arm's-length interest is exempt under s.212(1)(b); treaty rates for related-party interest are often 0% under Canada-US and Canada-UK treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation required when cross-border transactions with non-resident related persons exceed CAD 1,000,000 aggregate annual value (goods/services), with CAD 250,000 threshold for intangibles and financing transactions; Country-by-Country Report mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000. Canada has no de jure Local/Master File threshold, but CRA expects OECD-aligned documentation for material transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply the OECD Economic Substance Regulations used in Caribbean centers. CRA enforces the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Act s.245) and the substance-over-form doctrine. A Quebec LP must maintain genuine economic presence—physical office, local employees, management decisions, and business operations in Quebec—to preserve partnership status and claim treaty benefits. A hollow or shell LP can be re-characterized as a sham, its tax attributes ignored, and its partners treated as taxable in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of SaaS/SEO licensing revenues, false deductions for intercompany payments, concealed offshore bank accounts, or destruction of accounting records relating to the analytics tool's gross income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under s.239 Income Tax Act: fine of 50% to 200% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalty s.163(2): 50% of understated tax plus interest; equivalent Revenu Québec penalties apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and general partners can be assessed personally for withholding and source deductions and civil restitution. Criminal travel bans, passport surrender, and asset forfeiture may be imposed; principals face personal bankruptcy and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Billing below arm's length prices for the LP's proprietary SEO data feed, artificial management fees, or allocating R&D deductions to a non-resident affiliate to erode Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust prices under s.247(2) and impose a penalty under s.247(3) equal to 10% of the net adjustment where reasonable documentation is absent; interest on reassessments applies; secondary adjustments may be re-characterized as deemed dividends subject to Part XIII WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing documentation or create sham intercompany agreements may be personally fined up to CAD 50,000 on summary conviction, face civil restitution, and non-resident executives can be subject to entry bans during criminal investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Quebec LP without office, employees, or economic activity solely to reduce withholding rates, to access treaty benefits, or to defer tax by allocating profits to low-tax non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the claimed tax benefit under s.245(3); 25% GAAR penalty under s.245(5) in addition to tax and interest; possible re-characterization of the LP as a corporation; Revenu Québec may apply similar anti-avoidance rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner liability is unlimited; CRA may pierce the partnership veil and impose joint and several liability on directors and the general partner for tax, interest, and penalties; travel bans may be issued in egregious cross-border schemes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement AML compliance, accepting funds from sanctioned jurisdictions via Stripe or Paddle, failing to file suspicious transaction reports (STRs), or laundering crime proceeds through the SEO-SaaS revenue stream.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for unreported transactions; violations of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; criminal money-laundering conviction with imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for failing to discharge AML obligations; personal fines up to CAD 500,000 for indictable offences, 5-year travel ban, asset restraint, and imprisonment for complicity in money laundering.
